item.text: {"text":"Recent results support content-aware and time-aware sequential modeling, but the search did not identify a verified 2024–2026 paper matching every constraint: BERT4Rec, jointly learned title/description features, timestamp-aware attention, and no pretrained weights. [Improving Sequential Recommendations with LLMs (2024; revised 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01339) reports gains from LLM-initialized BERT4Rec embeddings, which require prohibited pretrained representations. [DenseRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18442) learns projections from pretrained content embeddings and reports improvements mainly from representing unseen history items; its experiments use SASRec, so it does not establish gains for the required architecture. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://dspace.hansung.ac.kr/bitstream/2024.oak/10390/2/AR_D2A1A2_ITS-Rec_%20A%20Sequential%20Recommendation%20Model%20Using%20Item%20Textual%20Information.pdf) combines textual features with sequential attention, but uses pretrained BERT and unavailable review text.\n\nFor temporal modeling, [TemProxRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09784) incorporates absolute/relative temporal and positional embeddings into attention, plus contrastive learning across interactions occurring near one another in time. It distinguishes short versus long interaction gaps and reports benchmark improvements. A constraint-compatible hypothesis—not a directly verified published recipe—is one BERT4Rec network combining item IDs with a small, randomly initialized token encoder over available titles/descriptions, trained jointly through masked-item prediction, plus bucketed time-gap attention biases. Retain reserved-mask training, appended-mask inference, and one checkpoint per category. Text and temporal additions need validation ablations: published gains involving pretrained semantics, external data, or different backbones do not establish improvement in this benchmark."}
